slots_and_copies.name: slot_sig_0x00
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Fixed offset 0x0000. 4-byte block header [u16 size=0x00DC][u16 checksum] + 220-byte payload whose first 16 bytes hold the clean-room-observed ASCII signature 'MarioGolfGBABUD\0'. Read/validated by FUN_080181c8 as the format-integrity marker: if the first 16 payload bytes mismatch a ROM-resident reference string, FUN_08018180 performs a full 8x0x1000 erase of the entire 0x8000 SRAM chip and FUN_080181c8 rewrites this block plus all others from scratch.

slots_and_copies.name: slot_main_0x41
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Fixed offset 0x0F00 in this sample. 4-byte header [u16 size=0x04D8][u16 checksum] + 1240-byte payload. Written by FUN_080181c8 via FUN_080180e4(0x41, buf, 0x4d8) as part of the same format/reset routine as slot_sig_0x00; contents in this sample are default/sentinel template data (par/hole-count/0xFF-sentinel 8-byte records and 4-byte sentinel records), not confirmed live gameplay data.

slots_and_copies.name: course_record_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: First of 7 consecutive 128-byte-spaced record blocks observed at file offsets 0x13E0, 0x1460, 0x14E0, 0x1560, 0x15E0, 0x1660, 0x16E0. Each is a 4-byte header [u16 size=0x0078][u16 checksum] + 120-byte payload. FUN_080181c8's reset path writes up to 20 such 120-byte blocks (2 outer x 2 mid x 5 inner loop, slot IDs 9..28+) via repeated FUN_080180e4 calls with size 0x78; only 7 are present/non-zero in this single sample, so the exact slot-ID-to-offset correspondence for the remaining ~13 is HYPOTHESIS only.

checksums.name: block_header_sum16
checksums.formula_detail: For a block with 4-byte header at offset B: size = u16_le(B+0..B+1); stored_checksum = u16_le(B+2..B+3); payload = bytes[B+4 : B+4+size]. computed = running 16-bit truncating sum ( (acc + word) & 0xFFFF ) of payload interpreted as little-endian u16 words (odd trailing byte, if any, added as its own byte value). Verified identical in both writer (FUN_08017fc0, variable iVar6) and reader (FUN_08017ec4, variable uVar7) decompiled loops.

io_driver_functions.notes: Raw byte-copy loop, param_1(src)->param_2(dst), param_3 bytes; used as the SRAM-side half of the verify-on-write cycle.
Second raw byte-copy loop used as the read-back/verify half after a write; returns comparison-ready buffer via func_0x08022bf4.

Write-then-verify-then-retry loop: calls FUN_0801e27c (write pass) and FUN_0801e2ec (read-back pass) up to 3 times until the result matches; standard SRAM robust-write pattern, no SRAM-specific bank/command bytes (0x5555/0x2AAA) observed anywhere in the traced code, ruling out Flash media.
Low-level SRAM/byte-addressable read primitive used by the block reader; no DMA3/EEPROM bit-serial pattern present.

Slot-ID lookup: scans a ROM-resident table (terminator byte 0x63/'99') matching the low byte of param_1 against each entry, returning a pointer whose +2 halfword is the SRAM byte offset for that slot. Table contents themselves are in ROM and not present in this workspace, so slot-ID -> offset mapping beyond the 3 directly-observed blocks is HYPOTHESIS.

Generic block reader: resolves slot via FUN_08017ea0, reads 4-byte header via FUN_0801e218, validates size < 0x1200, reads payload, computes sum16 checksum, compares to stored checksum, returns success/failure code.
Generic block writer: resolves slot via FUN_08017ea0, computes sum16 checksum over payload, assembles 4-byte header (size | checksum<<16), writes header+payload via FUN_0801e350.
Wrapper that calls FUN_08017fc0 twice: once for the plain slot id and once for (slot id | 0x100), i.e. writes a block and a second mirrored/alternate-base copy for redundancy.

Wrapper that reads the plain slot via FUN_08017ec4, then reads the (slot|0x100) mirror via FUN_08017ec4 again, and if both succeed re-writes the plain slot via FUN_08017fc0 -- a read+repair/resync routine.

Fills 8 x 0x1000-byte IWRAM buffers via an indirect function pointer (_DAT_080181c4, presumed memset-style fill) and writes each through func_0x0801e350 at offsets 0x0000, 0x1000, ... 0x7000 -- a full 0x8000 (32KB) SRAM erase/format pass.

Top-level format/integrity-check routine. Reads slot 0x00 and compares its first 16 payload bytes against a ROM-resident reference string; on mismatch it calls FUN_08018180 (full erase), then rewrites slot 0x00 (signature), slot 0x41 (main 1240-byte blob), and up to 20 per-record 120-byte blocks (slot ids derived from nested 2x2x5 loop counters + 9).

Highest traced caller of the save subsystem in this workspace; no caller found within the 205 sampled functions, so its invocation context (boot-time load vs. menu save) is UNKNOWN. Calls FUN_080181c8 (format check/repair) then FUN_0801811c(5, ...) to read slot 5, and copies resulting bytes into engine-state globals (sound/option byte flags) -- behavior consistent with a save-load-and-apply routine rather than a save-write routine.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Corrupt slot0_block_size (e.g. set to 0xFFFF or 0x0000) while leaving checksum and payload untouched.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: On next load, FUN_08017ec4's bounds check (`0x10 < uVar2` / `uVar2 < 0x1200` family of guards in the sibling 0x08015cf4-style readers, and the explicit size<0x1200 guard in FUN_08017ec4) should reject the block as invalid, triggering FUN_080181c8's mismatch path: a full 0x8000 SRAM erase and reformat of slots 0x00, 0x41, and the 7 course-record blocks. Verifiable by diffing a paired pre/post .ss save state and confirming all active ranges revert to the fresh-format pattern documented above.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one byte of the 'MarioGolfGBABUD\0' signature at offset 4 (e.g. offset 4 0x4d -> 0x00), leaving the stored checksum at offset 2 untouched (now stale/mismatched).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Checksum mismatch AND signature mismatch both fail; FUN_080181c8 should take its erase+reformat branch exactly as above. Distinguishing this from the pure-signature-mismatch-with-valid-checksum case (next target) isolates whether the checksum check or the signature compare is the actual gating condition in the live binary.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip the same signature byte at offset 4 but recompute and rewrite the stored checksum at offset 2 to match (sum16 over the mutated 220-byte payload).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If the engine's format check at FUN_080181c8 relies solely on the 16-byte signature compare (not the generic block checksum), this should still trigger the erase+reformat path even though the checksum now validates -- confirming the signature compare is an independent, additional integrity gate beyond the generic sum16 block checksum.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Overwrite the first 8-byte record of slot_0x41_record_array_8b (offset 0xfd4) with an out-of-range sentinel, e.g. holes field 0x0012 -> 0x0063 (99), leaving size/checksum stale.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: After repairing the slot_0x41 checksum, reload and observe (via paired .ss state RAM inspection) whether any code path reads this record into a bounded loop counter; an out-of-range 'holes' value could produce an observable out-of-bounds read/crash or a clamped default, falsifying or confirming the 'holes-per-course' hypothesis for this field.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set course_record_0's block size (offset 0x13E0) to 0x0000 while leaving its checksum stale.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: FUN_08017ec4 treats a decoded size of 0 as an error (`if (uVar2 == 0) iVar6 = 9;`), causing the read to fail for this specific record only; predict a localized reset of only this one 120-byte record on next relevant UI access (e.g. opening a course-select/records screen), NOT a full-chip erase, since this is a secondary slot distinct from slot 0x00's format-gate check in FUN_080181c8. This distinguishes 'local record corruption' handling from 'global format corruption' handling observed in targets above.

open_questions: The ROM-resident slot-ID lookup table read by FUN_08017ea0 is not present in this workspace; without it the mapping from numeric slot IDs (0x00, 0x41, and the ~20 course-record IDs computed in FUN_080181c8's nested loop) to the exact SRAM byte offsets is inferred only from the single available .sav file's byte layout, not proven from ROM data.

FUN_0801811c reads each slot twice -- once at the plain slot id and once at (slot id | 0x100) -- implying a second, alternate-base mirror copy of at least some blocks exists somewhere in the 32KB SRAM address space; this workspace's one .sav sample does not let us locate that mirror region, since the mirror's base offset (_DAT_08017fb8-style literals) is an unresolved ROM constant in the decompilation.

Only one real .sav file (saves/cap-00-future-0.sav) is present despite the packet's save-profile metadata mentioning 6 total_sav_files; cross-sample diffing (needed to confirm which fields change with actual gameplay vs. stay fixed as format template) could not be performed and is the single highest-value next step.

No paired .ss save states are present in this workspace (states/ is empty), so no RAM-mirror-to-SRAM-flush timing could be observed; the exact trigger event (course completion? menu confirm? auto-save?) that invokes FUN_080c9554 / the write path remains unconfirmed.

Semantic meaning of slot_0x41's three repeating template arrays (8-byte x52, 4-byte x36, 8-byte x9) and of the course-record 40-byte 1-4 value array is HYPOTHESIS only; no decompiled function in this workspace's 205-function sample names or indexes these specific sub-ranges by field.

FUN_080c9554 (the highest traced entry point into the save subsystem) has no caller within the 205 sampled functions, so whether it runs at boot, at save-file-select, or on an explicit in-game save action is UNKNOWN.
